annotations.text:
WHAT CHANGED FROM THE SKETCH

Dark throughout — black ground, amber accent carried over from B.

B's console voice folded into A's structure: mono for every number, a ~/free-llm prompt line instead of plain text filters, and a copy chip that appears on row hover so the base URL is one click away.

Real favicons back on every provider, on the same white/dark tile logic the live site uses — pale logos (Ollama, Cohere) get the dark tile so they don't vanish.

The hero gap now holds a rotating recommendation: five picks, one every 5s, with the killer number pulled out and a progress bar. Dots are clickable; the rotation speed is a tweak.

SEO STILL INTACT

The rotating card is decoration around the H1, not the H1 — the headline, the intro paragraph and the whole table render server-side in the HTML.

The table stays a real <table> with <thead>/<th>: that's what wins the "free LLM API rate limits" snippet.

Filter chips remain <a href> links to /?cat=… , so every filtered view is its own crawlable URL.

Only the rotation and the copy chip need JS.

B · CONSOLE — not chosen, but its voice moved into the final: mono data, amber accent, the prompt line, the copy-on-hover.

What stayed behind: the snippet panel driven by row selection. Worth revisiting for the provider pages, where it already exists.

C · INDEX — not chosen.

Still the best answer for long-tail SEO. The ranked framing and a real paragraph per provider are worth stealing for the /provider and /model pages, where there is room to breathe.
